finalText:
Based on my research, I now have comprehensive information about the `async` and `defer` attributes. Let me compile a complete answer.

## Complete Answer

The `async` and `defer` attributes on HTML `<script>` elements control when scripts are fetched and executed relative to HTML parsing and the DOMContentLoaded event. They have fundamentally different behaviors despite both allowing non-blocking fetches.

### The `async` Attribute

For external classic scripts, the `async` attribute causes the script to be "fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes)" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). This means the browser downloads the script without blocking HTML parsing, but executes it immediately upon completion, which can interrupt DOM construction. Importantly, `async` provides no guarantee about execution order when multiple scripts use this attribute; scripts execute in the order they finish downloading, not the order they appear in the HTML. Additionally, "scripts with an async attribute will execute as soon as the download is complete. This blocks the page and does not guarantee any specific execution order" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).

The `async` attribute "must not be used if the src attribute is absent (i.e., for inline scripts) for classic scripts, in this case it would have no effect" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).

### The `defer` Attribute

For external classic scripts, `defer` causes the script to be "fetched in parallel and evaluated when the page has finished parsing" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html). This means "scripts with a defer attribute will load in the order they are in and will only execute once everything has finished loading" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script). Critically, "Scripts with the defer attribute will execute in the order in which they appear in the document" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script), providing guaranteed execution order.

Like `async`, "This attribute must not be used if the src attribute is absent (i.e., for inline scripts), in this case it would have no effect" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).

### Interaction with HTML Parsing

The critical difference in parsing interaction is straightforward: `async` scripts are fetched in parallel but execute immediately when ready, potentially blocking the parser. `defer` scripts are also fetched in parallel but defer all execution until parsing is complete, never blocking the parser. Normal scripts without either attribute "block parsing until these are both complete" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

### DOMContentLoaded Event Timing

The DOMContentLoaded event fires at different points depending on script attributes. "The DOMContentLoaded event fires when the HTML document has been completely parsed, and all deferred scripts (<script defer src="…"> and <script type="module">) have downloaded and executed" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event). This means `defer` scripts execute before DOMContentLoaded fires, but "DOMContentLoaded is fired after the execution of these scripts, but before the execution of scripts with async" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/DOMContentLoaded_event).

### Inline Scripts

Inline scripts (scripts with inline content rather than a `src` attribute) are fundamentally different: `async` and `defer` attributes have no effect on them. Inline scripts with no type attribute execute immediately during HTML parsing, blocking the parser. However, "inline scripts with the type="module" attribute" do defer by default (https://web.dev/learn/performance/optimize-resource-loading).

### Module Scripts (`type="module"`)

Module scripts have special behavior. For module scripts, "if the async attribute is present, then the module script and all its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing, and the module script will be evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes). Otherwise, the module script and its dependencies will be fetched in parallel to parsing and evaluated when the page has finished parsing. (The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts.)" (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html).

This means module scripts defer by default—they behave like `defer` scripts without the `async` attribute. With `async`, they behave like async scripts. The key difference from classic scripts is that "The defer attribute has no effect on module scripts — they defer by default" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).

### When Both Attributes Are Specified

If both `async` and `defer` are specified, the `async` behavior takes precedence. "If the attribute is specified with the async attribute, the element will act as if only the async attribute is specified" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/script).
